situation.summary: Tenant Elena Voss reported on 12 Aug 2025 that a bedroom window at 24 Bramblewick Lane will not close or seal. The landlord, Dorian Pike, took over the repair himself after a delay over the insurance excess, and a visit was agreed for the morning of 29 Aug (E016). Nothing on record shows what happened at that visit. On 2 Sep the tenant said parts need ordering and a contractor would contact her the following week (E018). On 10 Sep she wrote "All jobs was done", said she had not told the agency because the contractor, Richard, would send a report (E020), and the landlord forwarded a gas safety record for a different property (E019). No contractor report or landlord confirmation shows the window now seals, so the completion claim is unverified and the case should not be closed.
situation.task: Verify whether the bedroom window repair is actually complete (the tenant says "all jobs was done"; the last recorded status is parts on order), before any close or landlord update.
situation.stageLabel: Completion claim to verify: landlord-managed window repair, parts reported on order (2 Sep), tenant says all done (10 Sep)
situation.whoseMove: Agency (Maya Chen) is the next mover; nobody has a promised date due today. NEXT ACTION: tenant.ask by email to Elena Voss, reply by Fri 12 Sep 2025, follow-up Mon 15 Sep 2025. Draft: "Subject: Your bedroom window, has the repair been completed? Hello Elena, thank you for your email of 10 September. Before we record the repair as complete, please reply by email by Friday 12 September 2025 with: 1) whether the bedroom window now closes and seals fully; 2) what Richard (the contractor) did and when, and whether any part is still to be ordered or fitted (your email of 2 September said parts needed ordering); 3) whether "all jobs" means only the bedroom window or other work too, and if other work, what; 4) Richard's contact name and number, and a copy of any report he sends you. Until the window seals fully, please keep it closed and tell us straight away if you cannot secure it or it gets worse. We have also asked the landlord for the outcome of his visit and the parts timescale, and we will write to you by Monday 15 September 2025 with what we know. On your question of 17 August about the calls: our records do not show which number those calls came from, so we cannot confirm it; we will contact you by email, or agree a call with you beforehand. Kind regards, Maya Chen, Property Manager, Northbridge Lettings." ALSO SEND (same turn, email to Dorian Pike, landlord): ask for (1) the outcome of the 29 Aug visit, (2) whether the window is repaired or parts are outstanding, with a fitting date, (3) Richard's full name, company, contact and any report, (4) whether other work is being done, since the tenant's "all jobs" suggests so; flag that the gas safety record he forwarded on 10 Sep is for 8 Thistledown Mews, Vellumby, not this property, and ask him to confirm whether it was sent in error (we will not file or forward it against this repair); and ask whether the insurance excess he raised on 13 Aug is still open. Reply by Fri 12 Sep 2025. Do not close, do not forward the gas record to the tenant, and do not tell either party the window is fixed until evidence is on record.

decision.message:
Subject: Bedroom window, 24 Bramblewick Lane – tenant reports work completed

Dear Dorian,

Elena wrote to us this evening (10 September) to say the work has been done. She mentioned that the contractor, Richard, said he would send a report. Her last update to us, on 2 September, was that parts needed to be ordered.

So that we can record the job correctly, please could you reply by Monday 15 September 2025 to confirm:
1) that the bedroom window has been repaired and now closes and seals fully, and roughly when the work was done;
2) whether a report from Richard is available. If it is, please forward a copy;
3) that you are paying the contractor directly, so there is no invoice for us to process. If there is an invoice for us, please send it as a PDF.

Separately: the Landlord Gas Safety Record you forwarded this morning is for 8 Thistledown Mews, Vellumby, not 24 Bramblewick Lane. Could you let us know whether it was sent in error? If you meant to send the current gas safety record for Bramblewick Lane, please send that instead. We will not file the Thistledown Mews record against this property.

We have also asked Elena to confirm that the window now seals properly. Once we have both confirmations we will close this request. If anything is still outstanding, please tell us what it is and when it is expected.

Kind regards,
Maya Chen
Property Manager, Northbridge Lettings
decision.rationale: The landlord took on this repair himself. He decided to inspect first (E014), the visit was agreed for 29 August (E016), and a contractor then dealt with the tenant directly (E018, E020). On a landlord-managed job we tell the other party when one side reports it fixed, and we close on the landlord's confirmation. The tenant now says "All jobs was done" (E020). Her last update, though, was that parts were on order (E018), and "all jobs" is vague. There is also no report or landlord confirmation on file. So we update the landlord and ask him for the confirmation we need to close. The gas safety record he forwarded is for a different address (E019, A1), so we query it instead of relying on it. In the same turn we ask the tenant directly whether the window now seals, because closing needs positive confirmation. No contractor is assigned, no spend is approved and nothing is due to us, so escalating is not needed.
decision.expectedOutcome: The landlord confirms the window is repaired, says he is paying the contractor directly and may forward Richard's report. He also explains or corrects the gas safety record. The tenant confirms the window closes and seals. The case can then be closed without payment.

decision.message:
Subject: Bedroom window, 24 Bramblewick Lane – tenant reports work complete

Dear Dorian,

Your tenant at 24 Bramblewick Lane emailed us this evening (10 September) to say the work has been done. She said she had not told us earlier because Richard, the contractor, said he would send a report. The last update we had, on 2 September, was that parts needed to be ordered.

As you arranged this repair yourself, please could you confirm by Friday 12 September:
1. That the bedroom window has been repaired and now closes and seals fully, and whether any parts or further visits are still outstanding.
2. Whether Richard's report has reached you. If it has, please forward a copy so we can keep it on file.
3. Whether you are paying the contractor directly or any invoice needs to come through us. We have not received an invoice.

Separately, the Landlord Gas Safety Record you forwarded today (reference NBL-009-GSR-25) is for 8 Thistledown Mews, Vellumby, not 24 Bramblewick Lane. Please could you let us know whether it was sent in error, and send the current record for 24 Bramblewick Lane if you meant to send that one. We will not file the record you sent against this property.

We have asked the tenant to confirm the window now works. We will keep the job open until we have confirmation from you both. If we have not heard back, we will contact you again on Monday 15 September.

Kind regards,
Maya Chen
Property Manager, Northbridge Lettings
decision.rationale: The landlord is managing this repair himself. He chose to inspect first and agreed to attend on 29 Aug (E014, E016), and the contractor came through him (E018). For a landlord-managed job, the manual says to close on the landlord's confirmation. The tenant now says "All jobs was done" (E020), but the last recorded status was that parts were to be ordered (E018). The landlord does not know what the tenant reported and has not confirmed anything himself. Telling him and asking him to confirm completion and how payment is being handled is the step that moves the case towards closing. His only recent message (E019) forwarded a gas record for a different property (A1). We need to query that because it conflicts with this case's address and he is the only one who can settle it. The tenant's wording is vague and may not mean the window seals, so in the same turn we ask her to confirm (refinement 7). Her concern about rain and cold (E013) means she also gets advice on what to do if the window still does not seal.
decision.expectedOutcome: The landlord confirms the window is repaired and says how the contractor is being paid (directly or through us), and either corrects or explains the gas record. The tenant confirms the window closes and seals. The case can then be closed.
